import java.util.Scanner;

public class Main {
    public static void main(String[] args) {
        Scanner scanner = new Scanner(System.in);
        long number = scanner.nextLong();

        long[] powers = new long[19];
        powers[0] = 1;
        for (int i = 1; i <= 18; i++) {
            powers[i] = powers[i - 1] * 10;
        }

        long[] sumPowers = new long[19];
        sumPowers[0] = 0;
        for (int i = 1; i <= 18; i++) {
            sumPowers[i] = sumPowers[i - 1] + powers[i];
        }

        int maxPower = 1;
        while (maxPower <= 18 && sumPowers[maxPower] <= number) {
            maxPower++;
        }
        maxPower--;

        int[] answer = {Integer.MAX_VALUE};

        dfs(maxPower, number, 0, powers, answer);

        System.out.println(answer[0]);
        scanner.close();
    }

    private static void dfs(int level, long currentNum, int cost, long[] powers, int[] answer) {
        if (currentNum == 0) {
            if (cost < answer[0]) {
                answer[0] = cost;
            }
            return;
        }
        if (level == 0) return;

        long base = powers[level];
        int i;
        for (i = (int) (-10); i * base <= currentNum; i++);
        // i is now the first value where i * base > currentNum, so decrement to get the last valid i
        i--;

        // First recursive call: i - 1
        long newNum1 = currentNum - (i - 1) * base;
        int newCost1 = cost + Math.abs(i - 1) * (level + 1);
        dfs(level - 1, newNum1, newCost1, powers, answer);

        // Second recursive call: i
        long newNum2 = currentNum - i * base;
        int newCost2 = cost + Math.abs(i) * (level + 1);
        dfs(level - 1, newNum2, newCost2, powers, answer);
    }
}
